business_problem: Zhiyi Technology needed to match millions of product images against millions of overseas social-media assets so merchants could use creator content and trend signals for cross-border product-selection decisions. The scale of 10 million product vectors versus 2 million social-media query vectors made full matching extremely expensive, and the existing approach limited both freshness and the size of the content pool.
solution_summary: Zhiyi Technology rebuilt its large-scale image-matching workflow on Alibaba Cloud MaxCompute vector search while preserving its own computer- vision models. Social-media images and product images are first cleaned and cropped so only the garment region is passed downstream, which reduces noise from people, backgrounds, and accessories. Zhiyi's self-developed CV model then labels the cropped images and generates feature vectors on GPU clusters. Instead of shipping those vectors into a separate external vector-retrieval stack, the company writes them directly into MaxCompute and uses VECTOR_SEARCH SQL to perform massive offline similarity matching. That lets the business keep the model layer in-house while outsourcing the heavy retrieval layer to managed infrastructure. The new pipeline lowers CPU and memory cost sharply, reduces operational burden, and makes high-frequency full matching practical enough for ongoing merchandising and trend-selection workflows.

solution_components.name: MaxCompute
solution_components.role: Runs the large-scale offline vector retrieval layer that matches product and social-media content in batch.

solution_components.name: GPU cluster
solution_components.role: Runs Zhiyi's self-developed CV models for garment detection, labeling, and feature-vector generation.

solution_components.name: Self-developed CV model
solution_components.role: Extracts clothing-region features and produces the vectors used for matching and trend analysis.

data_flow: Product and overseas social-media images are cleaned, cropped to the garment region, and then processed by Zhiyi's CV model on GPU clusters to generate vectors. Those vectors are written into MaxCompute, where VECTOR_SEARCH SQL performs batch similarity matching so merchandising teams can connect products with creator content and trend signals for product-selection decisions.
business_outcome: The MaxCompute-based workflow removed a major scaling bottleneck from Zhiyi's matching engine. At the same vector scale, CPU consumption fell by about 73% and memory consumption by about 93%, which reduced retrieval cost by more than 70% and made it feasible to rerun full matching more often so merchants can use fresher off-site trend signals in product-selection decisions.
metrics: production cutover finished in about two weeks
architecture_clues: The workflow deliberately separates computer-vision understanding from the retrieval layer so the customer keeps its own model assets.
Image preprocessing crops garment regions before embedding generation to reduce noise from background elements.
Vector retrieval is executed in MaxCompute with SQL semantics instead of a separately operated ANN infrastructure tier.
The pipeline is optimized for high-frequency full reruns so trend freshness can influence merchandising decisions.
